info.title: Artistic Hub API
info.description: Artistic Hub API: public catalog, customer accounts, cart, checkout and orders, and the admin API under /admin.

get.description: The default address comes first, then the newest.

post.description:
The customer's first address becomes the default automatically. Send `is_default: true` to make a
later one the default; the previous default then stops being the default.

put.description:
Only the customer's own addresses can be changed; any other id returns 404. Past orders keep their own copy.
Send `is_default: true` to make it the default (the previous one stops being default). Sending
`is_default: false` for the current default returns 422: make another address the default instead.

patch.description: The previous default stops being the default. Only the customer's own addresses; any other id returns 404.

get.description:
Shows current prices and stock. An item that can no longer be bought stays, with an `issue`, and is left
out of the subtotal. Before the first add the cart is empty.

post.description:
Adding a variant already in the cart increases its quantity. Only buyable variants can be added
(active, of an active product, in stock), and the cart's quantity cannot be more than the stock: 422.
post.summary: Add a variant to the cart

patch.description:
Lowering it always works. Raising it needs the variant to still be buyable, with enough stock: 422
otherwise. Only items in the customer's own cart can be changed; any other id returns 404.

delete.description: Only items in the customer's own cart can be removed; any other id returns 404.
delete.summary: Remove an item from the cart

get.description:
Checks everything the payment will check (the address is yours, the cart is not empty, every item can be
bought in its quantity) and returns the address, items and fare_breakup at current prices. Changes nothing.
422 names what to fix: `address_id`, `cart`, or each item as `items.N`.

post.description:
Runs the review checks again (same 422s), creates a pending order from the cart at current prices and
returns a Razorpay `payment_url` to redirect the browser to. The total is worked out here, never sent by
the client. Pressing Pay again for the same cart and address returns the same link while it is valid.
The cart and stock are unchanged until the payment is confirmed. 409 while the same checkout is still
being prepared; 503 when Razorpay cannot start the payment (try again).

get.description:
Customers only (no admins, no deleted accounts), paginated. Search matches name, email and phone.
The response also has `filters` (the filters applied, with defaults filled in) and
`filter_options` (the values `sort` accepts).

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

to.description: Number of the last item in the slice.

total.description: Total number of items being paginated.

get.description:
Placed orders only (payment confirmed), newest first, paginated; `status` narrows to one status. Pending or
failed checkouts are not listed: open them by order number instead. Each row is a summary; use the order
number to show the details. The response also has `filters` (as applied) and `filter_options` (the values
`status` accepts).

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

to.description: Number of the last item in the slice.

total.description: Total number of items being paginated.

get.description:
Any of your orders by its order number, including a pending or cancelled checkout: the payment result page
(where Razorpay returns with `?order=`) calls this. `status` is the order status and `payment.status` the
newest payment's status; while `payment.can_pay` is true, `payment.payment_url` can be opened again.
Another customer's order number returns 404.

Placed orders only (payment confirmed), paginated, newest first by default. Pending and failed checkouts
are not listed. Search matches order number, customer name, email and phone, and the delivery city;
`customer_id` (a customer's reference_id) shows only that customer's orders. The response also has
`filters` (as applied, with defaults filled in) and `filter_options` (the values `status` and `sort` accept).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Searches order number, customer name, email and phone, and the delivery city.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: A customer's reference_id (from the customer list): only their orders.

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

to.description: Number of the last item in the slice.

total.description: Total number of items being paginated.

get.description:
Any order by its order number, in any status (also a pending or failed checkout a customer asks about).
Everything the customer sees, plus `review_reason` (why it needs attention, e.g. paid when stock was short),
the customer's `reference_id`, the current `payment` and the earlier attempts (`payment_history`) with their Razorpay ids. Unknown numbers return 404.

put.description:
Needs the current password (422 on `current_password` when it is wrong) and a new one that differs from it.
Every other session is signed out; this one stays signed in. Limited to 6 attempts a minute.

message.const: Your password has been changed. Other devices have been signed out.

post.description:
Always answers the same, whether or not the email belongs to a customer account, so it never reveals which
emails exist. When it does, a link to the customer reset page is emailed; it expires in 60 minutes.

message.const: If an account exists for that email, we've sent a link to reset the password.

post.description:
Takes the `email` and `token` from the reset link and the new password. On success every session of the
account is signed out; sign in again with the new password. 422 on `token` when the link is invalid, used
or expired.

message.const: Your password has been reset. Sign in with your new password.

post.description:
Always answers the same, whether or not the email belongs to a admin account, so it never reveals which
emails exist. When it does, a link to the admin reset page is emailed; it expires in 60 minutes.

message.const: If an account exists for that email, we've sent a link to reset the password.

post.description:
Takes the `email` and `token` from the reset link and the new password. On success every session of the
account is signed out; sign in again with the new password. 422 on `token` when the link is invalid, used
or expired.

message.const: Your password has been reset. Sign in with your new password.

get.description:
Every product with its variants, photos and tags, paginated. Also returns `filters` (as applied)
and `filter_options`.

parameters.description: Searches product name and slug, and variant name and SKU.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
newest (default), name, price_low (lowest price first), price_high (highest first), stock_low (lowest total stock first). | | |---| | `newest`
| | `name`
| | `price_low`
By the product's lowest variant selling price. | | `price_high`
By the product's highest variant selling price. | | `stock_low`
By the total stock of all its variants, lowest first. |

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

to.description: Number of the last item in the slice.

total.description: Total number of items being paginated.

post.description: Upload photos first with POST /admin/uploads/variant-photos and send the returned ids as variants.*.photo_ids.
post.summary: Create a product with its variants

get.summary: View a product with its variants, photos and tags

put.description:
Send the whole product: variants with a `reference_id` are updated, without one are created, and variants not
sent are deleted. Turning the product off turns every variant off. Photos not sent are deleted with their files.
put.summary: Save a product with all its variants

delete.description: Deletes its variants, photos (and their files) and tag links. Past orders keep their own copy.

get.description:
One card per buyable variant (active, of an active product, in stock), paginated. Besides `data`, `links`
and `meta`, the response has `filters` (as applied), `filter_options`, `price_range` (lowest and highest
selling price of everything buyable, for the price slider) and `tag_counts` (how many buyable variants have
each tag, ignoring filters).
get.summary: List product variants for the shop

parameters.description: Searches variant and product names and descriptions, and tag names.

parameters.name: min_price
parameters.description: Selling price in rupees, e.g. "800" or "800.00".

parameters.name: max_price
parameters.description: Selling price in rupees; must not be below min_price.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
newest (default), price_low, price_high. | | |---| | `newest`
| | `price_low`
Selling price, lowest first. | | `price_high`

delete.description:
Removes it right away (outside the product form), with its photos and tag links. A product must keep at
least one variant (409). An id that is not this product's variant returns 404.

post.description: Sets the customer's name and profile details. A customer has one profile; sending this again returns 409.
multipart/form-data with an `avatar` file. Replaces any previous avatar. Returns the profile with the new `avatar_url`.

Creates an active customer account from email and password only. No token is returned: the
customer signs in next, then creates their profile.
Only customer accounts can sign in here; admin accounts get the same error as a wrong password.
Only admin accounts can sign in here; customer accounts get the same error as a wrong password.

post.summary: Create a tag. A name already used (ignoring case) returns 422

put.summary: Rename a tag (everywhere it is used)

delete.summary: Delete a tag. It is removed from every variant; the variants stay

post.description:
multipart/form-data with `photos[]`: 1 to 8 files. Stores each one, not yet attached to any variant, and
returns them in the order sent, each with its media `id` (send the ids in the product save under
variants.*.photo_ids) and `url` (for the preview). If any file is invalid, none is stored (422 names the
file, e.g. photos.2). Photos never attached to a variant are deleted automatically after 24 hours.

delete.description:
Deletes the photo and its file right away: one on a saved variant (its other photos keep their order), or
one uploaded and removed from the form before saving. Any admin can delete any variant photo; an id that is
not a variant photo returns 404.

Null when the item can be bought as it is. Otherwise unavailable (turned off), out_of_stock, or

stock.description: Units left: the most this item's quantity can be.

their rules are not decided yet (backend SRS, BE-CHECKOUT-02).

SaveProductRequest.description:
The whole product, sent on every save (create and update): product fields plus every variant it
should have. Variants with a `reference_id` are updated, without one are created, and variants not sent are
deleted. Photos are media ids returned by POST /admin/uploads/variant-photos, in display order.
Every id here is a client-facing reference id (ULID); toData() turns them into internal ids.

is_active.description: Turning the product off turns every variant off.

reference_id.description: The variant's reference_id; leave out for a new variant.

name.description: Unique within this product, ignoring case (other products may use the same name).

description.description: Falls back to the product description when null.

selling_price.description: Rupees, up to 2 decimals; must not be more than original_price.

photo_ids.description: 1 to 8 media ids per variant (from POST /admin/uploads/variant-photos), in display order; the first is the cover, the second the hover image.

SaveProductRequest.title: SaveProductRequest
